title: Written under French siege. It gave the world the word liberal.

beats.text: Written under French siege. It gave the world the word liberal.
1810. French armies held most of Spain. One city held out behind its walls: Cádiz.
beats.say: Eighteen-ten. French armies held most of Spain. One city held out behind its walls: Cádiz.

beats.text: With the king a prisoner in France, deputies from Spain and the Americas met there. Who ruled Spain now?
Their answer shocked the old world: the nation. Not the king.
On Saint Joseph's day, 1812, they proclaimed a constitution. Spaniards nicknamed it La Pepa.
beats.say: On Saint Joseph's day, eighteen-twelve, they proclaimed a constitution. Spaniards nicknamed it La Pepa.

beats.text: Power split in three. Votes for men. Its defenders called themselves liberales. The word spread across Europe.
Two years later, King Ferdinand came home, and tore it up.
In 1820, an officer named Rafael del Riego rebelled. The king was forced to swear loyalty to La Pepa.
beats.say: In eighteen-twenty, an officer named Rafael del Riego rebelled. The king was forced to swear loyalty to La Pepa.

beats.text: Three years later, a French army marched in to rescue the king. Riego was executed in Madrid.
La Pepa kept losing. But its ideas reached Portugal, Italy and Latin America.
